Be cautious. I was genuinely interested in Bible Note and spent some time reading through the privacy policy and looking into the company behind it. The app itself looks capable, but a few things gave me pause. Most notably, there is very little transparency about who is actually behind the organization, what theological oversight (if any) exists, or what doctrinal perspective guides its AI-generated content. While the privacy policy is fairly typical for an AI application, it does state that user-submitted content may be processed to improve its AI models after anonymization. None of this necessarily means the app is problematic, but for a Bible study tool, I would have expected much greater transparency about the people, theology, and governance behind it. For now, I’m remaining cautious.
